description: tools.get on a name that does not exist: -31911, and the refusal NAMES the nearest tool. A bare not-found would be a dead end, and the usual cause is a typo or an alias spelled from memory — tool names are authored in code, so there is a fixed set to be near. The sentence is the ADAPTER's, produced by the one layer that has read the registry and the rows, and the protocol door ships it untouched under its own code (a paraphrase at the door would be a second authority over a fact it cannot see). The same answer must never be an empty entry: an empty tool would be the plausible wrong answer, readable as "this tool does nothing".
